page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-focused x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. The configuration includes 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core with dedicated CPU allocation. It is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with instruction set extensions such as AVX, FMA, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local storage or attached GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested configurations with a stress-ng score of 2865.09. Multi-core performance aligns with average expectations in the middle 50%, recording a stress-ng score of 11559.23, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6531.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 12961.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 553.27 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 46.79 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Application benchmarks show average metrics across workloads, including 8.77 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 10.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 221.85 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M parameter LLM model.

From an engineering and resource design perspective, c2d-standard-8 delivers a balanced resource density without bundled local storage overhead. The high single-thread CPU performance paired with dedicated AMD EPYC cores makes it cost-efficient for workloads requiring predictable compute execution without requiring GPU hardware. Suitable target workloads include web serving, software compilation, database management operations, data compression tasks, and lightweight microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is an x86_64 compute instance equipped with an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor offering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 32.0 GB of system RAM. Featuring an instruction set with AVX, FMA, and AES cryptographic flags alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, the system does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core processing capabilities placing in the top 25% of benchmarks, alongside solid middle-tier multi-core, memory bandwidth, and caching metrics. Multi-threaded evaluations demonstrate average throughput across Redis operations, software compilation, and web serving. Given its predictable dedicated CPU allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c2d-standard-8 instance is suited for compute-oriented web applications, microservices, compilation jobs, and general-purpose database operations.
